items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: No direct interaction or relationship described between Charles Mingus and Eileen Southern in the transcript.

ctx.x: Well, yeah, Erroll Garner -- Martha Glaser told me he went to a concert in Carnegie Hall and went back upstairs, and his studio is upstairs, in Carnegie Hall (inaudible) upstairs, and sat down and played a whole piece through, because he remembered it. But that's how he learned, he couldn't read, he couldn't --
* 19th-Century pianist, born a slave, blind from birth, Viz: Eileen Southern, The Music of Black Americans; Langston Hughes, Black Magic.
